links.outcome: Reliance on correct versus incorrect AI advice; relative AI reliance and self-reliance among dermatologists
links.effect: Reliance stronger for correct than incorrect advice (t222=4.2; P<.001); mean relative AI reliance 10.04% and relative self-reliance 85.6%, i.e., high self-reliance, low AI reliance; accuracy improved only 1% with AI.
links.quote: Reliance on AI was stronger for correct advice than for incorrect advice (t<sub>222</sub>=4.2; P<.001; Cohen d=0.1).

links.outcome: Dermatologist accuracy with versus without AI support in lesion classification
links.effect: Accuracy improved significantly with AI support (t222=-3.3; P<.001) but only by an average of 1%.
links.quote: A 2-tailed t test revealed that participants' accuracy improved significantly with AI support (t<sub>222</sub>=-3.3; P<.001; Cohen d=4.5), but only by an average of 1% (1/100).

unlisted_practices: Tailor AI decision support design to user experience level and propensity to trust technology

screen.reason: An experimental web-based reader study evaluating how psychological factors and experience influence dermatologists' reliance on an AI decision support tool.
